rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Detailing everything” may describe all the events of Joseph’s story with his father and brothers.
rows.anchor: المراد وتفصيل كل شيء من واقعة يوسف عليه السلام مع أبيه وإخوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers the description to concern the Qur’an as a whole, whose religious contents include lawful and unlawful matters.
rows.anchor: فإن جعل هذا الوصف وصفا لكل القرآن أليق من جعله وصفا لقصة يوسف وحدها

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: On either interpretation, the general wording intends a restricted subset, as in God’s mercy encompassing everything that can receive it.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي على التفسيرين جميعا : فهو من العام الذي أريد به الخاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an guides believers in this world and brings mercy in the resurrection; believers are named because they alone benefit from it.
rows.anchor: كونها هدى في الدنيا وسببا لحصول الرحمة في القيامة لقوم يؤمنون خصهم بالذكر

none: End-of-sūrah colophon, elegy, and next-sūrah heading; no interpretive point.

rows.speaker: النحويون
rows.claim: Subḥān is a verbal noun used as a proper name for glorification; glorifying God means declaring Him free of every defect.
rows.anchor: قال النحويون : { سبحان } اسم علم للتسبيح يقال : سبحت الله تسبيحا وسبحانا

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The root of tasbīḥ means distance, so to glorify God is to set Him apart from what is unbefitting.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( النظم ) : السبح في اللغة التباعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ can mean prayer: the people called glorifiers in 37:143 are worshippers, and supererogatory prayer is called subḥa because prayer magnifies and purifies God.
rows.anchor: أن التسبيح يذكر بمعنى الصلاة ، ومنه قوله تعالى : { فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ can mean making an exception, as in 68:28; invoking God’s will in an exception also expresses His exaltedness.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : ورد التسبيح بمعنى الاستثناء في قوله تعالى : { قال أوسطهم ألم أقل لكم لولا تسبحون }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: In the hadith about the “subuḥāt” of God’s face, the phrase means the light of His face.
rows.anchor: قيل معناه نور وجهه ، وقيل : سبحات وجهه ، نور وجهه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is the face’s radiance that makes a viewer say “Glory be to God.”
rows.anchor: نور وجهه الذي إذا رآه الرائي قال : سبحان الله

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Asrā and sarā are two lexical forms with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { أسرى } قال أهل اللغة : أسرى وسرى لغتان

rows.speaker: أجمع المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators agree that “His servant” refers to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أجمع المفسرون على أن المراد محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم سليمان الأنصاري
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Razi’s father says Muhammad answered that his highest honor was being attributed to God through servanthood.
rows.anchor: سمعت الشيخ الإمام أبا القاسم سليمان الأنصاري قال : لما وصل محمد صلوات الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laylan is in the accusative as an adverb of time.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { ليلا } نصب على الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite “a night” indicates only part of the night, emphasizing the short duration of the journey from Mecca to Syria, a forty-night route.
rows.anchor: أراد بقوله : { ليلا } بلفظ التنكير تقليل مدة الإسراء

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil dates the journey to one year before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : كان ذلك الليل قبل الهجرة بسنة

rows.speaker: أنس والحسن
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf transmits from Anas and al-Hasan that it occurred before the prophetic mission.
rows.anchor: ونقل صاحب ( الكشاف ) عن أنس والحسن أنه كان ذلك قبل البعثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report places Muhammad in the sanctuary’s Hijr, between sleeping and waking, when Gabriel came with the Buraq.
rows.anchor: روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( بينا أنا في المسجد الحرام في الحجر عند البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the journey began at Umm Hani’s house; on this reading, “the Sacred Mosque” means the surrounding sanctuary.
rows.anchor: وقيل أسري به من دار أم هانيء بنت أبي طالب . والمراد على هذا القول بالمسجد الحرام الحرم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the whole sanctuary counts as a mosque, a view Razi calls the majority position.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس الحرم كله مسجد ، وهذا قول الأكثرين

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The Farthest Mosque is Jerusalem’s Temple, called “farthest” because it lies far from the Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: اتفقوا على أن المراد منه بيت المقدس وسمي بالأقصى لبعد المسافة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The area around the Farthest Mosque was blessed with fruits and flowers.
rows.anchor: قيل بالثمار والأزهار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the area was blessed as the abode of prophets and the place where angels descend.
rows.anchor: وقيل بسبب أنه مقر الأنبياء ومهبط الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition “to” marks the journey’s endpoint; the verse does not say whether Muhammad entered the mosque.
rows.anchor: مدلول قوله : { إلى المسجد الأقصى } أنه وصل إلى حد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “To show him some of Our signs” refers to the marvels Muhammad saw that night, which attest to God’s power.
rows.anchor: يعني ما رأى في تلك الليلة من العجائب والآيات التي تدل على قدرة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: المعترضون
rows.claim: An objection says that “some” makes Muhammad’s vision partial, while Abraham saw the whole kingdom of the heavens and earth, apparently making Abraham’s ascent superior.
rows.anchor: فإن قالوا : قوله : { لنريه من ءاياتنا } يدل على أنه تعالى ما أراه إلا بعض الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that Abraham saw the kingdom of the heavens and earth, whereas Muhammad saw some of God’s signs, and God’s signs are superior.
rows.anchor: قلنا : الذي رآه إبراهيم ملكوت السموات والأرض ، والذي رآه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بعض آيات الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears Muhammad’s words, sees his acts, and knows their sincerity, so He singled him out for these honors.
rows.anchor: السميع لأقوال محمد ، البصير بأفعاله ، العالم بكونها مهذبة خالصة عن شوائب الرياء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, God hears what people say about the Messenger and sees what they do in this event.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد سميع لما يقولون للرسول في هذا الأمر ، بصير بما يعملون في هذه الواقعة

rows.speaker: الأكثرون من طوائف المسلمين
rows.claim: Most Muslim groups hold that Muhammad’s body as well as his spirit made the journey.
rows.anchor: الأكثرون من طوائف المسلمين اتفقوا على أنه أسرى بجسد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: A report al-Tabari attributes to Hudhayfa treats the event as a dream in which Muhammad’s body was not absent.
rows.anchor: حكي عن محمد بن جرير الطبري في ( تفسيره ) عن حذيفة أنه قال ذلك رؤيا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: The spirit-only or dream interpretation is also attributed to Aisha.
rows.anchor: وحكي هذا القول أيضا عن عائشة رضي الله عنها

rows.speaker: معاوية
rows.claim: The spirit-only or dream interpretation is also attributed to Muawiya.
rows.anchor: وعن معاوية رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi separates the question whether the rapid movement was rationally possible from whether it actually occurred.
rows.anchor: الكلام في هذا الباب يقع في مقامين : أحدهما : في إثبات الجواز العقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sphere’s near half-revolution in a night, together with the circumference-to-diameter ratio, shows that ascending beyond the highest sphere within a fraction of a night is possible.
rows.anchor: وقد ثبت في الهندسة أن نسبة القطر الواحد إلى الدور نسبة الواحد إلى ثلاثة وسبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun’s disk is about 160 times Earth’s size, yet sunrise occurs quickly; this shows that very rapid motion is possible.
rows.anchor: ثبت في الهندسة أن قرص الشمس يساوي كرة الأرض مائة وستين وكذا مرة ثم إنا نشاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a dense body’s rapid ascent is impossible, the equally rapid descent of a subtle spiritual body such as Gabriel would also be impossible, undermining prophecy; the majority regard Gabriel as a moving body.
rows.anchor: فإن كان القول بمرعاج محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في الليلة الواحدة ممتنعا في العقول

rows.speaker: الحكماء
rows.claim: Philosophers interpret Gabriel’s descent as bodily veils lifting from Muhammad’s spirit so it perceives what is manifest to Gabriel.
rows.anchor: قلنا : تفسير الوحي بهذا الوجه هو قول الحكماء ، فأما جمهور المسلمين فهم مقرون بأن جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام جسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects that spiritualized account as the philosophers’ position; most Muslims take Gabriel’s descent to mean physical movement from the celestial realm to Mecca.
rows.anchor: فأما جمهور المسلمين فهم مقرون بأن جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام جسم وأن نزوله عبارة عن انتقاله

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: When people challenged the ascent report, Abu Bakr affirmed that Muhammad spoke truth; Razi says belief in his prophethood warrants accepting this lesser marvel.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو بكر : إن كان قد قال ذلك فهو صادق ، ثم جاء إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who regard Satan as a subtle body already accept his swift travel from east to west to tempt humans; such movement is even more fitting for eminent prophets.
rows.anchor: الوجه الرابع : أن أكثر أرباب الملل والنحل يسلمون وجود إبليس ويسلمون أنه هو الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This analogy applies to people who regard Satan as a body; it does not address those who regard him as an immaterial evil spirit, though most religious groups consider him a subtle, moving body.
rows.anchor: أما الذين يقولون إنه من الأرواح الخبيثة الشريرة وأنه ليس بجسم ولا جسماني ، فهذا الإلزام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that a dense human body cannot move as quickly as angels or devils confuses the general possibility of rapid movement with the separate question of its occurrence in a human body.
rows.anchor: نحن إنما استدللنا بأحوال الملائكة والشياطين على أن حصول حركة منتهية في السرعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an says Solomon’s wind traveled a month’s journey in morning and evening, and observation likewise shows winds crossing great distances rapidly.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى في صفلا مسير سليمان عليه الصلاة والسلام : { غدوها شهر ورواحها شهر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person with knowledge of the Book brought Bilqis’s throne from Yemen to Syria in the blink of an eye, showing that such movement is possible for a human.
rows.anchor: قال الذى عنده علم من الكتاب أنا ءاتيك به قبل أن يرتد إليك طرفك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the theory that vision sends a ray from the eye to its object, seeing someone entails a ray’s rapid transit and thus demonstrates that such speed is possible.
rows.anchor: الوجه السابع : إن من الناس من يقول : الحيوان إنما يبصر المبصرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because bodies are alike in their essential natures, rapid movement possible for some bodies is possible for Muhammad’s body too.
rows.anchor: أنا بينا بالدلائل القطعية أن الأجسام متماثلة في تمام ماهياتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God can do every possible thing, the bodily ascent is possible; mere amazement cannot refute it without also refuting other miracles.
rows.anchor: ثبت بالدليل أن خالق العالم قادر على كل الممكنات ، وثبت أن حصول الحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi compares the ascent’s strangeness with Moses’ staff becoming a huge serpent and a small staff again, a she-camel emerging from rock, and a mountain suspended in air.
rows.anchor: فإن كان مجرد التعجب يوجب الإنكار والدفع ، لزم الجزم بفساد القول بإثبات المعجزات

rows.speaker: أهل التحقيق
rows.claim: The Qur’an and hadith establish that God carried Muhammad’s body and spirit from Mecca to the Farthest Mosque; “servant” denotes both together.
rows.anchor: قال أهل التحقيق : الذي يدل على أنه تعالى أسرى بروح محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وجسده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who identify the human being with the spirit argue that the self remains one while bodily parts continually change.
rows.anchor: أما القائلون بأن الإنسان هو الروح وحده ، فقد احتجوا عليه بوجوه : أحدها : أن الإنسان شيء واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second argument says people know their own selves even when unaware of their bodily parts, so self and body differ.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : إن الإنسان قد يكون عارفا بذاته المخصوصة حال ما يكون غافلا عن جميع أجزائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third argument notes that people call their hands, legs, brain, and heart “mine,” implying a self distinct from those organs.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أن الإنسان يقول بمقتضى فطرته السليمة يدي ورجلي ودماغي وقلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that ordinary self-reference is not decisive; reason shows one agent uses the hand, eye, and ear as instruments, distinct from those organs.
rows.anchor: قلنا : نحن لا نتمسك بمجرد اللفظ حتى يلزمنا ما ذكرتموه ، بل إنما نتمسك بمحض العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a person is the spirit alone, “His servant” in the verse refers to the spirit and does not prove that the body traveled.
rows.anchor: المراد من العبد جوهر الروح وعلى هذا التقرير فلم يبقى في الآية دلالة على حصول الإسراء بالجسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says a spirit-only ascent is ordinary, so it would not suit the declaration “Glory be to Him”; Razi answers that unprecedented spiritual unveilings could still merit it.
rows.anchor: فإن قالوا : فالإسرا بالروح ليس بأمر مخالف للعادة ، فلا يليق به أن يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues that “servant” denotes body and spirit together, as it does of a person praying in 96:9–10 and God’s servant calling upon Him in 72:19.
rows.anchor: والجواب : أن لفظ العبد لا يتناول إلا مجموع الروح والجسد ، والدليل عليه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well-known sound hadith also describes travel from Mecca to Jerusalem and then from there to the heavens.
rows.anchor: وأما الخبر فهو الحديث المروي في الصحاح وهو مشهور وهو يدل على الذهاب من مكة إلى بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: المنكرون
rows.claim: Three rational objections claim that this speed is inconceivable, a heavy body cannot ascend to the heavens, and ascent would burn the celestial spheres.
rows.anchor: أحدها : بالوجوه العقلية وهي ثلاثة : أولها : أن الحركة البالغة في السرعة إلى هذا الحد غير معقولة

rows.speaker: المنكرون
rows.claim: They argue that an unseen miracle of this magnitude would be pointless, since it should have occurred publicly to prove Muhammad’s prophethood.
rows.anchor: والشبهة الثانية : أن هذا المعنى لو صح لكان أعظم من سائر المعجزات

rows.speaker: المنكرون
rows.claim: They read the “vision” that became a trial for people in 17:60 as the ascension, concluding that it was a dream.
rows.anchor: تمسكوا بقوله : { وما جعلنا الرءيا التى أريناك إلا فتنة للناس }

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The hadith’s reduction of fifty prayers to five after Moses’ intercession would entail abrogation before an obligation took effect and divine change, which the Qadi deems impossible.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : وهذا يقتضي نسخ الحكم قبل حضوره ، وأنه يوجب البداء وذلك على الله تعالى محال

rows.speaker: المنكرون
rows.claim: They also reject details such as washing the split chest with Zamzam and riding the Buraq, which they consider unnecessary or ineffective.
rows.anchor: منها ما روي من شق بطنه وتطهيره بما زمزم وهو بعيد ، لأن الذي يمكن غسله بالماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The display of signs benefited Muhammad: seeing Paradise and Hell beforehand would lessen their shock at judgment and leave him free to intercede.
rows.anchor: أن خيرات الجنة عطيمة ، وأهوال النار شديدة ، فلو أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام ما شاهدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His vision of prophets and angels on the night of ascent could complete his own benefit or theirs.
rows.anchor: لا يمتنع أن تكون مشاهدته ليلة المعراج للأنبياء والملائكة ، صارت سببا لتكامل مصلحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing the heavens, Throne, and celestial conditions could make worldly hardships seem small and strengthen Muhammad’s resolve in preaching and struggle.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أنه لا يبعد أنه إذا صعد الفلك وشاهد أحوال السموات والكرسي والعرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “to show him some of Our signs” indicates that the journey’s benefit was specifically for Muhammad.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن قوله : { لنريه من ءاياتنا } كالدلالة على أن فائدة ذلك الإسراءة مختصة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi will explain at 17:60 that the vision was an actual seeing, not a dream.
rows.anchor: نبين أن تلك الرؤيا رؤيا عيان لا رؤيا منام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s actions are not subject to objection: He does what He wills and rules as He desires.
rows.anchor: لا اعتراض على الله تعالى في أفعاله فهو يفعل ما يشاء ويحكم ما يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse alone does not prove ascent to the heavens or beyond the Throne; others cite the opening of al-Najm, 84:19, or the hadith.
rows.anchor: المسألة الرابعة : أما العروج إلى السموات وإلى ما فوق العرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage shifts from third-person narration to direct address and back, a rhetorical device called الالتفات.
rows.anchor: انتقل من الغيبة إلى الخطاب ومن الخطاب إلى الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning Muhammad’s honor through the night journey, God mentions Moses’ prior honor through the revealed Torah.
rows.anchor: المسألة الثانية : ذكر الله تعالى في الآية الأولى إكرامه محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن أسرى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah guides by leading the Israelites from ignorance and unbelief to knowledge and true religion.
rows.anchor: يخرجهم بواسطة ذلك الكتاب من ظلمات الجهل والكفر إلى نور العلم والدين الحق

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads “that you take” with a yāʾ, speaking about the Israelites in the third person; the other readers use the direct-address tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو : { ألا تتخذوا } بالياء خبرا عن بني إسرائيل والباقون بالتاء

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: One grammatical reading makes an subjunctive and gives the sense “so that you do not take.”
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي : إن قوله : { ألا تتخذوا } فيه ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها : أن تكون

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: A second reading takes an as explanatory “that is,” with a shift from narration to direct address, as in 38:6.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أن تكون ( أن ) بمعنى أي التي للتفسير وانصرف الكلام من الغيبة إلى الخطاب

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: A third reading treats an as extra and supplies an unspoken command: “We said, do not take anyone besides Me as trustee.”
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أن تكون ( أن ) زائدة ويجعل تتخذوا على القول المضمر والتقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wakīl is a lord to whom people entrust their affairs.
rows.anchor: البحث الثالث : قوله : { وكيلا } أي ربا تكلون أموركم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence links Muhammad’s ascent and Moses’ Torah to the Torah’s call to monotheism: the highest rank is exclusive reliance on God, with speech, thought, and desire devoted to Him.
rows.anchor: لا معراج أعلى ولا درجة أشرف ولا منقبة أعظم من أن يصير المرء غرقا في بحر التوحيد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes “progeny of those We carried with Noah” as a vocative addressed to the Israelites; this works on the direct-address reading.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول مجاهد لأنه قال : هذا نداء قال الواحدي : وإنما يصح هذا على قراءة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says all people descend from Noah, who sailed with his three sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : الناس كلهم ذرية نوح لأنه كان معه في السفينة ثلاثة بنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parsing makes “progeny” the object of “take”: do not take Noah’s descendants as trustees besides God.
rows.anchor: أن الاتخاذ فعل يتعدى إلى مفعولين كقوله : { واتخذ الله إبراهيم خليلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A grateful servant” means Noah gave thanks abundantly.
rows.anchor: أي كان كثير الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Noah thanked God after eating, drinking, dressing, putting on shoes, and relieving himself, recognizing God could have withheld each comfort.
rows.anchor: روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان إذا أكل قال : ( الحمد لله الذي أطعمني ولو شاء أجاعني )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Noah offered his food to the believers before breaking his fast and gave it to anyone in need.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه كان إذا أراد الإفطار عرض طعامه على من آمن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praise of Noah explains the prohibition on associating partners: gratitude means recognizing every blessing as God’s favor, so his descendants should follow him.
rows.anchor: لا تتخذوا من دوني وكيلا ولا تشركوا بي ، لأن نوحا عليه الصلاة والسلام كان عبدا شكورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recalling the gift of Torah, Razi says God explains that the Israelites failed to follow it and instead committed corruption twice.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر إنعامه على بني إسرائيل بإنزال التوراة عليهم ، وبأنه جعل التوراة هدى لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadāʾ linguistically means cutting or deciding something with precision; here “We decreed” means God informed and revealed the matter to them, with ilā linked to revelation.
rows.anchor: القضاء في اللغة عبارة عن قطع الأشياء عن إحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their promised corruption means sins and violating Torah’s commands, in the land of Egypt; their great elevation means unjust domination over people.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { لتفسدن } يريد المعاصي وخلاف أحكام التوراة وقوله : { في الأرض } يعني أرض مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the first punishment was due, God sent people of great military strength, with baʾs meaning fighting and the dispatch also meaning God left Israel without aid.
rows.anchor: ومعنى بعثنا عليكم أرسلنا عليكم ، وخلينا بينكم وبينهم خاذلين إياكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One historical account identifies the attackers as Nebuchadnezzar after Israel’s first corruption: he killed prophets, slaughtered people, killed 40,000 Torah readers, and exiled the rest to Babylon.
rows.anchor: فسلط الله عليهم بختنصر فقتل منهم أربعين ألفا ممن يقرأ التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that account, another king later married an Israelite woman, returned the Israelites to Jerusalem at her request, and Israel recovered its former good condition.
rows.anchor: تزوج بامرأة من بني إسرائيل فطلبت تلك المرأة من ذلك الملك أن يرد بني إسرائيل إلى بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second account identifies the attackers as Goliath’s forces; the returned victory is Saul’s strength against Goliath and David’s killing him.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : إن المراد من قوله : { بعثنا عليكم عبادا لنا } أن الله تعالى سلط عليهم جالوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third account says God removed the Israelites’ fear from the Magians’ hearts, allowing them to attack and devastate Israel when sins multiplied.
rows.anchor: والقول الثالث : إن قوله : { بعثنا عليكم عبادا لنا } هو أنه تعالى ألقى الرعب من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says identifying the attackers is not central; the lesson is that persistent sin brought armies that killed and destroyed Israel.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه لا يتعلق كثير غرض في معرفة أولئك الأقوام بأعيانهم ، بل المقصود هو أنهم

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth defines jāsū as moving back and forth through homes in a destructive manner; khilāl means the gaps between things.
rows.anchor: قال الليث : الجوس والجوسان التردد خلال الديار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses jāsū as searching through the homes.
rows.anchor: فعن ابن عباس فتشوا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses jāsū as looking for the people inside.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : طلبوا من فيها

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses jāsū as ravaging and corrupting the homes.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة : عاثوا وأفسدوا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says they went through the homes to check whether anyone remained whom they had not killed.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : طافوا خلال الديار هل بقي أحد لم يقتلوه

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi says the root means movement and searching and can encompass all the reported glosses.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : الجوس هو التردد والطلب وذلك محتمل لكل ما قالوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fulfilled promise is God’s irrevocable, certain decree; the returned “turn” means restored power and rule, and nafir means the number of men.
rows.anchor: ثم قال تعالى : { وكان وعدا مفعولا } أي كان قضاء الله بذلك قضاء جزما حتما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafir is the number of men who rally with a man from his clan; it is synonymous with nāfir, like qadīr and qādir.
rows.anchor: النفير العدد من الرجال وأصله من نفر مع الرجل من عشيرته وقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ashʿarites argue that God’s certain decree that Israel would corrupt means their not doing so would make God’s true knowledge, truthful report, and firm judgment false; their acts were therefore inevitable despite being forbidden.
rows.anchor: عدم وقوع ذلك الفساد عنهم يستلزم انقلاب خبر الله تعالى الصدق كذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They further argue that God says He sent the attackers who killed, plundered, and captured Israelites, attributing sinful injustice to God and thus grounding good and evil in His decree.
rows.anchor: فبين تعالى أنه هو الذي بعثهم على بني إسرائيل ، ولا شك أن قتل بني إسرائيل ونهب

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī answers that God ordered the attackers to campaign because Israel was corrupt.
rows.anchor: المراد من { بعثنا عليكم } هو أنه تعالى أمر أولئك الأقوام بغزو بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī alternatively takes “We sent” to mean that God let them attack and did not place fear of Israel in their hearts.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أن يكون المراد خلينا بينهم وبين بني إسرائيل ، وما ألقينا الخوف من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the command interpretation: attackers who destroyed Jerusalem, burned the Torah, and killed its guardians cannot plausibly have acted by God’s command.
rows.anchor: الذين قصدوا تخريب بيت المقدس وإحراق التوراة وقتل حفاظ التوراة لا يجوز أن يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also rejects equating sending with mere nonintervention, since sending means empowering and inciting, while leaving alone is omission—the opposite kind of act.
rows.anchor: البعث على الفعل عبارة عن التقوية عليه وإلقاء الدواعي القوية في القلب ، وأما التخلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites’ obedience restored their rule after punishment, so good deeds benefit themselves and persistence in sin harms themselves; reason recognizes self-benefit as good and self-harm as blameworthy.
rows.anchor: فعند ذلك ظهر أنهم إن أطاعوا فقد أحسنوا إلى أنفسهم ، وإن أصروا على المعصية فقد أساؤا

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi supplies an implied “We said”: obedience opens blessings and good things, while forbidden acts open punishment.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : لا بد ههنا من إضمار ، والتقدير : وقلنا إن أحسنتم أحسنتم لأنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun in “for it” creates a parallel construction and means “to it” or “against it”; Arabic prepositions may substitute for one another.
rows.anchor: قال النحويون : إنما قال : { وإن أسأتم فلها } للتقابل والمعنى : فإليها أو فعليها

rows.speaker: أهل الإشارات
rows.claim: The people of allusion infer that mercy outweighs wrath because the verse repeats the good deed twice but mentions the evil only once.
rows.anchor: قال أهل الإشارات هذه الآية تدل على أن رحمة الله تعالى غالبة على غضبه بدليل أنه

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: They identify the later promised punishment with Israel’s killing Zechariah and John; al-Wahidi says Nebuchadnezzar then enslaved and killed them and destroyed Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : معناه وعد المرة الأخيرة ، وهذه المرة الأخيرة هي إقدامهم على قتل زكريا ويحيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects that chronology: Nebuchadnezzar lived long before Jesus, John, and Zechariah, and he says the later avenging king was the Roman Constantine; exact identities are not needed for exegesis.
rows.anchor: التواريخ تشهد بأن بختنصر كان قبل وقت عيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام ويحيى وزكريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted answer to “when the later promise comes” is “We send them,” understood from the earlier statement that God sent attackers.
rows.anchor: المسألة الثانية : جواب قوله : { فإذا جاء } محذوف تقديره : فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb “grieve” is attributed to faces because inner joy appears as radiance, while grief and fear appear as a dark, grim face.
rows.anchor: آثار الأعراض النفسانية الحاصلة في القلب إنما تظهر على الوجه

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: The common reading has the plural third-person “that they may grieve,” matching the attackers as the agents and the following plural verb.
rows.anchor: قرأ العامة : ليسوؤا على صيغة المغايبة ، قال الواحدي : وهي موافقة للمعنى

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: Ibn Amir, Abu Bakr from Asim, and Hamza read the singular “that he may grieve”; its subject may be God, the attack, or the promise.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم وحمزة : { * ليسوء } على إسناد الفعل إلى الواحد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj identifies the singular verb’s subject as the promise, which grieves their faces.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : ليسوء الوعد وجوهكم

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi reads the first-person plural “that We may grieve,” attributing the act to God as in the surrounding verbs.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي بالنون وهذا على إسناد الفعل إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabbara means to perish, while tabbarahu means to smash or destroy; “what they overcame” can mean what they conquered or all the while they ruled.
rows.anchor: يقال : تبر الشيء تبرا إذا هلك وتبره أهلكه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says tabbara is to make something broken and fragmented, as with broken glass or gold.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : كل شيء جعلته مكسرا ومفتتا فقد تبرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic verbal noun tatbīran confirms and removes doubt about the promised destruction, as in “God spoke to Moses directly.”
rows.anchor: وقوله : { تتبيرا } ذكر للمصدر على معنى تحقيق الخبر وإزالة الشك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may show mercy and pardon the Israelites after punishing them.
rows.anchor: ثم قال تعالى : { عسى ربكم أن يرحمكم } والمعنى : لعل ربكم أن يرحمكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they return to sin, God will again send worldly punishment as a chastisement and warning; further relapse brings renewed calamity.
rows.anchor: فإن عدتم مرة أخرى إلى المعصية عدنا إلى صب البلاء عليكم في الدنيا مرة أخرى

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal reads the warning as worldly punishment, linking it to God’s declaration that He would send someone to afflict Israel until Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : إنما حملنا هذه الآية على عذاب الدنيا لقوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: He says Israel again sinned by rejecting Muhammad and concealing the Torah and Gospel, so Arabs punished them; Nadir, Qurayza, Qaynuqa, and Khaybar were killed or expelled, with survivors subdued by poll tax.
rows.anchor: أي وإنهم قد عادوا إلى فعل ما لا ينبغي وهو التكذيب لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaṣīr can mean Hell is the one enclosing the unbelievers or that it is their confined place.
rows.anchor: والحصير فعيل فيحتمل أن يكون بمعنى الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly punishment can be escaped through death or otherwise, but Hell surrounds people permanently with no possibility of release.
rows.anchor: وأما عذاب الآخرة فإنه يكون حاصرا للإنسان محيطا به لا رجاء في الخلاص عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage contrasts honors for the obedient—Muhammad’s journey and Moses’ scripture—with punishments for the rebellious, then praises the Qur’an: obedience brings good and disobedience calamity.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك تنبيها على أن طاعة الله توجب كل خير وكرامة ومعصيته توجب كل بلية وغرامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an calls this religion “most upright,” while another verse calls Abraham’s religion upright; comparison would require degrees of truth, so “more upright” is figurative, an elative used for a plain adjective, or the familiar superlative.
rows.anchor: قولنا هذا الشيء أقوم من ذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative phrase “that which is most upright” omits its noun, understood as the religion, law, or path, as in the “better way” of 41:34.
rows.anchor: قوله : { للتى هى أقوم } نعت لموصوف محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s guidance leads to soundest belief and best conduct, so it brings believers who act righteously a great reward.
rows.anchor: أنه يبشر الذين يعملون الصالحات بالأجر الكبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soundest path must yield the greatest profit and benefit.
rows.anchor: الطريق الأقوم لا بد وأن يفيد الربح الأكبر والنفع الأعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third Qur’anic quality is painful punishment for those who reject the hereafter; rejecting right belief and conduct brings the greatest harm.
rows.anchor: فكذلك تركه يوجب لتاركه الضرر الأعظم الأكمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the disbelievers’ punishment is conjoined to the promise of reward: believers receive the reward and hear that their enemies will be punished.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن قوله : { وأن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة } عطف على قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling punishment “good news” is either sarcastic or an opposite-term expression, as when a like-for-like requital of evil is called evil.
rows.anchor: مذكور على سبيل التهكم ، أو يقال : إنه من باب إطلاق اسم الضدين على الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the passage concerns Jews, Razi says most Jews deny bodily reward and punishment, while others claimed Hell would touch them only for a few days; both views resemble rejecting the hereafter.
rows.anchor: أن أكثر اليهود ينكرون الثواب والعقاب الجسمانيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s coherence is that people may turn away from the Qur’an’s laws and explanations despite receiving this great divine gift, and pursue what brings no benefit.
rows.anchor: بعد أن أنزل الله عليه القرآن وخصه بهذه النعمة العظيمة والكرامة الكاملة ، قد يعدل عن التمسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the person calling for evil as al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who invoked God to bring the claimed truth and was answered by execution; others demanded punishment or asked when the threat would come.
rows.anchor: القول الأول : المراد منه : النضر بن الحرث حيث قال : { اللهم إن كان هاذا هو الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says angry people curse themselves, family, children, and property; if evil prayers were granted as readily as good ones, they would perish.
rows.anchor: المراد أنه في وقت الضجر يلعن نفسه وأهله وولده وماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet prayed that Sawda’s hand be cut after she loosened a captive’s restraints, then explained that an undeserved angry prayer against family becomes mercy; he told her to lower her raised hand.
rows.anchor: فقال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( اللهم اقطع يدها ) فرفعت سودة يدها تتوقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi proposes that people may eagerly ask for what they think good although it is harmful, because haste and surface appearances keep them from investigating its reality.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المراد : أن الإنسان قد يبالغ في الدعاء طلبا لشيء يعتقد أن خيره فيه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the written muṣḥaf omits the expected wāw in yadʿu because it is not pronounced; it remains understood grammatically, like other omitted letters, and spelling it would also be correct.
rows.anchor: البحث الرابع : القياس : إثبات الواو في قوله : { ويدع } إلا أنه حذف في المصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omission of a few letters in the written text while others remain proves the Qur’an was preserved as heard, with no human editorial changes.
rows.anchor: فإن إثبات الياء والواو في أكثر ألفاظ القرآن وعدم إثباتهما في هذه المواضع المعدودة يدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says “the human” means Adam: when the spirit reached his navel, he admired his body and tried to rise before he could, showing haste.
rows.anchor: القول الأول : آدم عليه السلام ، وذلك لأنه لما انتهت الروح إلى سرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other view takes “the human” generically: everyone is prone to haste, though abandoning it would improve religion and worldly life; Razi says this is the underlying point even if Adam is intended.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : أنه محمول على الجنس ، لأن أحدا من الناس لا يعرى عن عجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One coherence reading follows the Qur’an’s religious blessings with worldly blessings: as the Qur’an combines clear and ambiguous passages, time combines day and night, both needed for complete benefit.
rows.anchor: لما بين في الآية المتقدمة ما أوصل إلى الخلق من نعم الدين وهو القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second coherence reading says the previous verse’s “most upright” guidance presents proof of monotheism and prophethood, so this verse follows with cosmic signs.
rows.anchor: ذلك الأقوم ليس إلا ذكر الدلائل الدالة على التوحيد والنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third coherence reading links human haste and constant changes of state with the world’s alternation between light and darkness and the moon’s waxing and waning.
rows.anchor: لما وصف الإنسان بكونه عجولا أي منتقلا من صفة إلى صفة ومن حالة إلى حالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the night and day themselves as the two signs: their continual alternation despite their opposition proves that a creator governs them.
rows.anchor: القول الأول : أن يكون المراد من الآيتين نفس الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day also serve worldly needs: night provides rest, while daylight enables earning and managing livelihood.
rows.anchor: فلولا الليل لما حصل السكون والراحة ، ولولا النهار لما حصل الكسب والتصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, the construct “sign of the night/day” is explanatory: night itself is the erased sign, and day itself is the illuminating sign, like saying a thing’s very essence.
rows.anchor: ثم قال تعالى : { فمحونا ءاية اليل } وعلى هذا القول : تكون الإضافة
